Pre-op clearance includes a face-to-face airway, heart, lung, and allergy evaluation before surgery.

body.text: Patients researching surgery in Istanbul often spend weeks scrutinizing their surgeon's credentials while overlooking the physician responsible for their breathing, heart rate, and safe awakening. At [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/), our two founders help clients plan realistic pre-op appointment buffers without taking commissions from any hospital or surgeon. We coordinate your visit. Your licensed medical team makes clinical decisions.
Who administers general anesthesia and IV sedation legally in Türkiye?

Under Turkish healthcare regulations, general anesthesia and deep intravenous sedation must be administered and supervised by a board-specialized physician—an Anesthesiology and Reanimation Specialist (Anesteziyoloji ve Reanimasyon Uzmanı)—holding a medical degree plus specialist residency training. Anesthesia technicians assist only under the direct supervision of that specialist physician.

The national professional body representing these physicians is the [Turkish Society of Anesthesiology and Reanimation (TARD)](https://www.tard.org.tr/), which has been a member society of the [World Federation of Societies of Anaesthesiologists (WFSA)](https://wfsahq.org/member-focus/about-our-members/member-societies/turkey/) since 1964. Before consenting to any procedure involving general anesthesia or IV sedation, ask for the named anesthesiologist's full name and confirm that they will remain physically present throughout induction, surgery, and initial recovery.
What pre-op cardiac, lung and allergy checks happen the morning before surgery?

Standard pre-anesthesia evaluation follows international perioperative frameworks such as the [American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) Practice Advisory for Preanesthesia Evaluation](https://journals.lww.com/anesthesiology/fulltext/10.1097/00000542-200202000-00037~practice-advisory-for-preanesthesia-evaluation-a-report-by) and its [updated ASA guidance](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22273990/). At minimum, the anesthesiologist reviews your medical history and conducts a focused physical exam covering your airway, lungs, heart, vital signs, and drug allergies.

Depending on your age, medical history, and the invasiveness of the operation, your hospital team may order selective blood panels (complete blood count, coagulation, biochemistry), an electrocardiogram (ECG), or a chest X-ray, and request internal medicine or cardiology clearance when risk factors appear. Arriving in Istanbul at least one full day before surgery gives your team time to complete blood draws and consultations without rushing on the morning of the operation.

body.text: What questions should you ask the anesthesiologist directly?

Every patient undergoing general anesthesia or IV sedation should meet the anesthesiologist face to face before entering the operating room. Preparing five direct questions helps confirm who is monitoring you, how fasting rules apply, and how nausea or post-op pain will be managed safely.
Bring these written questions to your pre-op anesthesia consultation:

items: Specialist identity: "Are you the board-certified Anesthesiology and Reanimation Specialist managing my case from start to recovery?"
Medication holds: "Which of my regular medications, supplements, or GLP-1 injections must be paused, and for how many days?"
Fasting window: "What is my exact cutoff time for solid food and clear water?"
Monitoring & ICU backup: "What continuous monitoring is used in the operating room, and is an intensive care unit (ICU) on site in this hospital?"
Post-op comfort plan: "What protocol do you use for post-anesthesia nausea, shivering, and pain control in the first 24 hours?"

body.text: Why should general anesthesia NEVER occur in an unequipped office clinic?

General anesthesia and deep sedation depress spontaneous breathing and blood pressure; if an unexpected airway obstruction, severe allergic reaction, or malignant hyperthermia occurs, survival depends on immediate access to hospital-grade anesthesia machines, piped medical gases, emergency resuscitation drugs, blood-bank access, and an on-site intensive care unit.

Office-based consultation suites and small outpatient dental or aesthetic rooms lack full hospital backup. If a clinic proposes performing a procedure requiring general anesthesia in a private office rather than a licensed full-service hospital, decline and walk away. faq.q: Can a surgeon or dentist administer general anesthesia themselves in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. General anesthesia must be administered and supervised by a licensed Anesthesiology and Reanimation Specialist physician separate from the operating surgeon or dentist.

faq.q: Should I fly into Istanbul the same morning as a general anesthesia procedure?
faq.a: No. Arriving at least 24 hours early allows rest, hydration, unhurried blood tests, and an in-person pre-anesthesia evaluation before fasting begins.

faq.q: What if my pre-op blood test or ECG shows an unexpected abnormality?
faq.a: Your anesthesiologist has full clinical authority to delay or cancel elective surgery until a specialist evaluates the finding. Build flexible hotel and flight terms into your trip plan.

faq.q: Do I need to disclose vaping, smoking, or herbal supplements to the anesthesiologist?
faq.a: Yes. Nicotine, alcohol, herbal supplements, and weight-loss medications can directly affect airway reactivity, bleeding, and stomach emptying under anesthesia.

faq.q: Is IV sedation ("twilight sleep") safe in a small office without an anesthesiologist?
faq.a: Deep IV sedation carries airway and breathing risks similar to general anesthesia and should be managed by a qualified anesthesia specialist in a properly equipped clinical setting.

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye select or vet my anesthesiologist?
faq.a: No. We organize your travel, accommodation, and appointment logistics independently; verifying clinical credentials and making all medical decisions remain strictly between you and your licensed medical team.
